# Get-ADGroupMembershipReport

<!-- Generated by tools/Build-Catalog.ps1. Edit the script header, not this file. -->

Audits Active Directory group membership and writes an HTML report (optional CSV).

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `scripts/windows/active-directory/Get-ADGroupMembershipReport.ps1` |
| Platform | Windows (RSAT ActiveDirectory module, domain-joined machine) |
| Permissions | Read-only domain user (standard users can read group membership) |
| Safety | Read-only |

## When to use

Access reviews, audits of who is in which security group, or before cleaning up groups.

## Description

For each group named in -GroupNames (or every group matching -GroupNameFilter) lists the members with their type,
name, SamAccountName, enabled state, title, department, last logon and manager (users only). Disabled users and
distribution groups are skipped unless requested, and -Recursive expands nested groups. The HTML report has one
row per group member; -ExportCsv adds a CSV with the same data plus group category, scope, last logon and manager.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-OutputPath` | String | No | Folder for the report. Falls back to $env:TOOLBOX_REPORT_DIR, then prompts. |
| `-CustomerName` | String | No | Optional. Adds a &lt;OutputPath&gt;\&lt;CustomerName&gt; subfolder. |
| `-GroupNames` | String[] | No | Optional. Names of the groups to audit. If omitted, groups are selected with -GroupNameFilter. |
| `-GroupNameFilter` | String | No | Filter on group Name used when -GroupNames is not given. Default '*' (all groups). '*' is the only wildcard; all other characters, including quotes, parentheses and backslashes, are matched literally. |
| `-ExportCsv` | SwitchParameter | No | Also write a CSV next to the HTML report. |
| `-Recursive` | SwitchParameter | No | Expand nested group membership. |
| `-IncludeDisabledUsers` | SwitchParameter | No | Include disabled user accounts (skipped by default). |
| `-IncludeDistributionGroups` | SwitchParameter | No | Include distribution groups (skipped by default; only security groups are audited). |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Get-ADGroupMembershipReport.ps1 -GroupNames 'Domain Admins','Server Operators' -OutputPath D:\Reports
```

```powershell
.\Get-ADGroupMembershipReport.ps1 -GroupNameFilter 'SG-*' -Recursive -IncludeDisabledUsers -ExportCsv -OutputPath D:\Reports -CustomerName Contoso
```
